shadows.name: engrave

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: Crates drawer; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: tube-flash
motion.value: --flash += 0.55 + overshoot on transient, decays x0.78 per meter frame

motion.name: rust
motion.purpose: Corrosion overlay opacity, weep length 70-180px, drip scaleY 0.55-1.

motion.name: lights-out
motion.purpose: Birthday reveal; removed under reduced motion.

stage.behaviour: Fixed artboard scaled whole to the window; no breakpoints.

narrative.overview:
The instrument is a wall, not a panel with a skin. Every surface is board-formed concrete, cold Owens grey, split into slabs by black shadow gaps. Controls are either cut into that concrete (lettering, wells, fader slots, the scope screen) or bolted onto it (matte black cast knobs, the caged tube, anchor bolts). Nothing floats, nothing glows except what the sound lights.

There is one accent, rust coral, and it only ever means value or signal: knob arcs, fader fills, the tube, the scope trace, the active state. The wall decays on demand. The RUST macro writes a live `--rust` (0 to 1) that raises a corrosion overlay from slab edges, lengthens the weeps under anchor holes, and stretches the drips under the RUST knob. The caged fluorescent tube is the output meter and flashes on transients, and the overhead spill light washes down the wall with it.

The stage is a fixed 1200 x 750 artboard scaled whole to the plugin window. Density is high but every control is large and decisive; the giant RUST knob and the largest CUTOFF knob anchor the hierarchy.
keyCharacteristics: Board-formed concrete slabs on a near-black ground, 4px shadow gaps.
Engraved lettering: bone fill clipped through the concrete texture, dark top lip, light bottom lip.
One accent, rust coral, reserved for value and signal.
Matte black cast knobs from a single raster plate; coral SVG arcs and bone needles drawn on top.
Material that reacts: tube level and flash, overhead spill, RUST corrosion.

rules.name: The One Rust Rule
rules.body: Coral marks value, signal, or selection. It is never decoration, never a panel fill, never a heading colour.

rules.name: The Wash-Not-Filter Rule
rules.body: Concrete is cooled and darkened inside its own background layers, never with a CSS filter on the slab, because a slab filter dulls the knobs and lettering bolted to it.

rules.name: The Engraved Rule
rules.body: Lettering on concrete is cut, not printed: engrave-fill over the concrete plate (300px tile) clipped to the glyphs, text fill transparent, a 1px dark drop-shadow above (rgba(0,0,0,0.7)) and a 1px light one below (rgba(236,228,214,0.14)). Applies to the wordmark, slab heads, knob and fader labels, bench tabs and selector positions. Live values inside a label break out in hot coral.

rules.name: The Lit-Glass Exception
rules.body: Labels on the dark scope screen are lit, not cut: plain dust bone with a black text shadow.

rules.name: The Tracked Caps Rule
rules.body: All UI text is uppercase and tracked; tracking grows with importance (0.1em controls, 0.2em labels, 0.3em tabs and preset name). Lowercase appears only in user-entered content: tags, notes, search.

rules.name: The Overhead Light Rule
rules.body: Top edges of cuts are dark, bottom edges catch light. Never invert it, never light from the side.

dos: **Do** cut every word that sits on concrete using the Engraved Rule; break live values out in hot coral.
**Do** keep coral for values, signal and selection only.
**Do** mark a selected control with hot coral text or a 2px coral rule, never with a filled coral block (paper chips excepted).
**Do** drive any new decay or reaction from `--rust`, `--level` and `--flash` rather than new timers.
**Do** cool and darken concrete in its background layers, keeping filters off slabs.
**Do** keep everything on the fixed 1200 x 750 stage and scale the whole.
donts: **Don't** print flat light text for wall lettering (slab heads, control labels, tabs); it reads as a skin, which is what the world refuses. Lists and inputs inside the crates drawer and labels on the scope glass are read, not carved, and stay flat.
**Don't** add a second accent hue or tint panels with coral.
**Don't** add light sources beyond the tube, its overhead spill and the scope phosphor.
**Don't** set the wordmark face anywhere but the wordmark.
